states.content: Nina Reed is Marcus Reed's sister and drove him to the cardiology rhythm clinic today. She helped with intake and previously could help with parking and arrival times if Marcus's schedule changes, and she needed appointment times to know whether to take off work. Her family logistics access is revoked: she is not to receive future appointment details, procedure times, or callback instructions, and Marcus is taking over the logistics himself from here. Marcus specifically asked that the Friday, March 13 TEE-guided cardioversion scheduling details be sent only to him in the portal and not to Nina.

states.content: Family logistics access for Nina Reed is revoked: future appointment details, procedure times, and callback instructions must not be shared with Nina Reed. Marcus specifically requests that the Friday, March 13 TEE-guided cardioversion scheduling details (12:30 PM procedure, 11:00 AM arrival) be sent only to him in the portal and not to Nina. Previously, through Monday, only logistical information (arrival times, where Marcus needs to go, basic transportation instructions) could be shared with Nina, while medication changes, lab results, adherence history, and chart notes were restricted; the clinical reason for schedule changes was also not to be disclosed. Marcus does not want details of his recovery discussed with family, and nurse Jamison agreed to keep family updates within the logistics scope he set. The TEE-guided cardioversion wording is acceptable in Marcus's portal copy but must not be used in family or voicemail messages. Marcus also does not want another patient or another family member to hear his schedule or contact notes, and wants his chart kept separate from other patients' charts. A same-surname caution note has been added to the desk workflow, and his restricted contact note stays on his chart only.

states.content: Cardioversion remains the plan for Marcus Reed's atrial fibrillation rhythm control. Because the timing of his Monday-night apixaban dose is uncertain, Dr. Patel is changing the approach from direct cardioversion to TEE-guided cardioversion so a clot can be checked for first while still avoiding an unnecessary delay. The Wednesday, March 11 slot was released, and the Thursday, March 12 slot was taken by an add-on case; the TEE-guided cardioversion is now scheduled for Friday, March 13 at 12:30 PM with 11:00 AM arrival at the cardiac procedures unit. Scheduler Terry has updated the arrival letter in the portal, and Marcus's own portal copy prep line now says TEE-guided cardioversion. Marcus requests that the procedure slot details be put in the chart. Dr. Patel has reviewed the labs and stated they are acceptable for outpatient cardioversion, satisfying the pending-labs condition; full medication history reconciliation remains part of the plan. Dr. Patel instructs that Marcus must not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion, and to continue apixaban exactly as prescribed without missing any further doses. Pharmacist Klein confirms apixaban stays at 5 mg twice daily and Marcus must not stop or skip it on his own unless the cardiologist specifically says otherwise. The only routine periprocedural hold discussed is lisinopril on the morning of the procedure once the date is confirmed. Nurse Jamison will bring Marcus back first for his cardiology rhythm clinic visit.

He asks that the Cedar Bridge number not be called unless his cell fails; the Cedar Bridge front desk stops routing calls after 5 PM, so daytime backup contact through the front desk (617-555-0140) is limited to daytime, and if his cell 617-555-0104 fails after 5 PM the Cedar Bridge evening desk at 617-555-0162 is the after-hours backup number, recorded only as a backup after-hours route. He does not want his cell number used if someone needs to discuss the procedure or his heart rhythm. Backup contact details are not needed unless cardiology requests them. Messages should use generic callback wording only, asking them to have Marcus call Riverside Cardiology back, and must not mention cardioversion, atrial fibrillation, blood thinner, or recovery housing. Routine reminders should go to the patient portal whenever possible. Marcus is fine with the portal wording saying TEE-guided cardioversion, but does not want that wording used in family or voicemail messages.
